note: A single pull-in site on a gravel lot in full sun directly beside paved PA 144, on the left three tenths of a mile past Penrose. The agency calls it traditionally a hunting campsite and says to expect road noise in exchange for the easy access. No table, toilet or water. Pack out trash. --Claude
summary: Site page re-read: SS006 still listed, Drive-In, category Trailer Site only (ruling 4), max vehicle 25 ft (equipment length 35), gravel pull-in on PA 144; count 1 and 25 ft confirmed, pull_through false and a sites note added. Season year-round confirmed; Available on every night probed. Fees confirmed, $6.50 reservation fee added; hookups and facilities none. Imagery (Esri): gravel lot about 35 x 50 m off the north-west side of the paved highway, pin on it; not moved. NHD: nothing within 200 m; not waterfront.
flags: Agency access statements (ruling 11: nothing measured): the page carries the standard 'Caution: This campsite is accessed by remote state forest dirt or gravel roads and may not be suitable for some low-clearance vehicles or large RVs.' although its own description puts the site on PA 144 ('Road noise to be expected but provides easy access'); imagery shows the lot opening straight onto the paved highway, so the caution was left out of the note as boilerplate that does not describe this site. No grade given; no Severe grade, 4WD, wet-weather or clearance statement. Kept. Boilerplate on every Sproul page, not site-specific: 'State forest roads are not maintained in the winter and often become snow covered, icy and potentially impassable' and '4WD vehicles may be recommended for some sites year-round, check notes' (this site's notes say nothing about 4WD).
Category: 'Looking For Category: Trailer Site' only, no RV or Tent category (ruling 4: listed for trailers and long enough, stays). GIS record TrailerAccess 'Yes'.

ATV check (ruling 1): nothing on the site page or GIS record calls this lot ATV parking. The DCNR Bloody Skillet ATV Trail brochure (rev. 4/14/16) shows three ATV parking areas: the northern trailhead (41.14139,-77.78694), the middle lot (41.12417,-77.77944) and the southern lot at Orviston (41.10161,-77.74763). The 2026 advisory also names a 'Route 144' parking lot, which the 2016 brochure does not show and no page read locates. Because this site is a gravel lot on PA 144, it could not be ruled out from the pages read that the unlocated 'Route 144' ATV lot is this one; the brochure's nearest lot, the northern trailhead, is about 8 km south-south-east of this pin. Kept as no agency page names it; the district office (570-923-6011) could settle it.

Sproul advisories page (read 2026-11-10): no closure or restriction on this site's road; it carries the Bloody Skillet Orviston-lot section closure, the indefinite Left Branch Young Womans Creek Road closure, 'Stay Alert for ATVs on Roads', a dust advisory and a firewood-cutting road list.

NAME: the '(Snow Shoe)' in the stored name is only the booking system's loop label ('Site, Loop: SS006, Snow Shoe'). It is on PA 144 three tenths of a mile past Penrose. Suggest a name that says where it is; apply.py does not write names.

Agency pages disagree on the district's own inventory: the Sproul camping page says 'Sproul State Forest offers nine roadside campsites for overnight camping in RVs. No tent camping permitted. Self-contained toilets are required.' while the district's 2025 map labels CR001-CR021 plus the WS series, and the CR booking pages list 'Tent Site, Trailer Site'. Nothing here depends on it.
